records.title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention
records.text_en: When several persons commit a criminal act in furtherance of a common intention, each of them is liable as if the act were done by him alone.

records.title: Punishment of qatl-i-amd
records.chapter: Of offences affecting the human body
records.text_en: Whoever commits qatl-i-amd is liable to qisas, or to death or imprisonment for life as tazir, depending on the circumstances.
records.punishment: Qisas, or death or imprisonment for life as tazir

records.title: Punishment for theft
records.text_en: Whoever commits theft is punishable with imprisonment of either description for up to three years, or with fine, or with both.
records.punishment: Up to 3 years, or fine, or both

records.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
records.text_en: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces a person to deliver property is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years and fine.

records.title: Punishment for criminal intimidation
records.chapter: Of criminal intimidation, insult and annoyance
records.text_en: Whoever commits criminal intimidation, meaning threatening a person with injury to person, reputation or property, is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
records.punishment: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both

records.title: Arrest how made
records.text_en: In making an arrest the police officer or other person making it shall actually touch or confine the body of the person to be arrested, unless the person submits to custody by word or action. No more restraint than necessary may be used.

records.title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail
records.text_en: A police officer arresting a person without warrant must immediately tell the person the full particulars of the offence, and, if the arrest is not for a non-bailable offence, that the person is entitled to be released on bail.

records.title: When police may arrest without warrant
records.text_en: A police officer may arrest without an order from a magistrate and without a warrant any person who has been concerned in a cognizable offence, or against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, or credible information received, or a reasonable suspicion exists of such involvement.

records.title: Person arrested not to be detained more than twenty-four hours
records.text_en: No police officer shall detain in custody a person arrested without warrant for longer than is reasonable, and such period shall not exceed twenty-four hours, excluding travel time to the magistrate's court, without the order of a magistrate under section 167.

records.title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR)
records.text_en: Information about a cognizable offence given orally to the officer in charge of a police station shall be written down, read over to the informant and signed by the informant, and a copy shall be given to the informant free of cost.

records.title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours
records.text_en: When a person is arrested and the investigation cannot be completed within twenty-four hours, the police must produce the person before the nearest magistrate with a copy of the diary entries. The magistrate may authorise detention in custody for a limited time.

records.title: In what cases bail to be taken
records.text_en: When a person who is not accused of a non-bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant by a police officer, or appears before a court, and is prepared to give bail, that person shall be released on bail.

records.title: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
records.text_en: A person accused of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail by the court, but not where there appear reasonable grounds for believing he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years. Special rules apply to women, children and the sick.
